question: Two times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 41 years. After 7 years, nine times Q’s age will be 24 years less than six times P’s age at that time. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present condition: 2P − Q = 41.

Condition after 7 years: 9(Q + 7) = 6(P + 7) − 24 ⇒ 9Q + 63 = 6P + 18.

Rearranging and dividing by 3, we get: 2P − 3Q = 15.

Subtract this from the first equation: (2P − Q) − (2P − 3Q) = 41 − 15.

⇒ 2Q = 26 ⇒ Q = 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two times P's present age exceeds Q's present age by 41 years.

After 7 years, 9 times Q's age is 24 less than 6 times P's age.

 
 Present Age
 P = P, Q = Q
 2P − Q = 41
 
 

 

 +7 Years
 
 
 After 7 Years
 P = P+7, Q = Q+7
 9(Q+7) = 6(P+7) − 24
 
 Solving gives Q = 13 years

**Calculations:**

Let the present age of P be P and Q be Q.

⇒ 2P − Q = 41

⇒ 2P = Q + 41 --- (Equation 1)

After 7 years, P's age = P + 7 and Q's age = Q + 7.

According to the second condition:

⇒ 9(Q + 7) = 6(P + 7) − 24

⇒ 9Q + 63 = 6P + 42 − 24

⇒ 9Q + 63 = 6P + 18

⇒ 9Q + 45 = 6P

Dividing the equation by 3:

⇒ 3Q + 15 = 2P

Substitute 2P from Equation 1:

⇒ 3Q + 15 = Q + 41

⇒ 2Q = 26

⇒ Q = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ages Concept Basic Rule

Always assume the present age as a variable (like x). The age 't' years ago will be (x − t) and 't' years hence will be (x + t).

Linear Equations Method

When solving two equations, equate the coefficients of one variable and subtract or add to eliminate it, finding the value of the other variable quickly.

Ratio Difference Approach

If the age ratio changes from a:b to c:d over 't' years, we can use the cross-multiplication method to quickly find the present age parts instead of solving full equations.
